items.title: Doubling an admissible hypercube matching profile into a perfect admissible tuple
items.author: Joshua Erde
items.work: Matchings in the hypercube with specified edges
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Lemma l:admissible at source lines 67-69: if x in N^n is an admissible profile and the new coordinate satisfies x_{n+1} = 2^n - 2||x||_1, then the concatenated tuple (2x, x_{n+1}) must be a perfect admissible tuple. The adjacent proof at source lines 70-84 has to construct the matching in the right ambient cube: it takes two disjoint copies of a matching M_1 with profile x inside Q^{n+1} (lines 71-76), then uses exactly the vertex set X of Q^n left uncovered by M_1, whose size is 2^n - 2||x||_1 = x_{n+1}, to add the direction-e_{n+1} edges joining the two copies of every uncovered vertex (lines 78-81). Both conclusions must then be checked, namely that M_3 is a matching with profile (2x, x_{n+1}) and that it is perfect because 2||x||_1 + |X| = 2^n (line 83). The step that is not a routine verification is the choice of the leftover set and the dimension, which makes the new coordinate absorb precisely the uncovered vertices; the argument is short and elementary once that choice is made, so it is rated H2.
